topic: What if the internet just disappeared forever without warning?

script.text: Day six. Everyone's phone has turned into a camera with a flashlight. But yours is different. Before that flight, you didn't just download music. You downloaded the whole of Wikipedia. Almost seven million articles, with pictures, about a hundred gigabytes. You did it because you were bored.
Now you're carrying the biggest library in town in your pocket. How to purify water. How to treat a burn. How to fix an engine. How to grow potatoes.

Word gets around. People knock on your door with questions, and you read them the answers. The farmer down the road. A nurse. A guy whose solar panels won't talk to his battery anymore. You start writing the answers on paper, and pinning them to the library door.
A little boy asks how to make his grandad's old radio work. You find the page, and ten minutes later it crackles to life.

Then, on the seventh evening, a black car pulls up outside. There's no traffic anymore, so you hear it from three streets away. A man in a grey suit gets out. His shoes are clean. Nobody's shoes are clean anymore. He doesn't knock. He just waits until you open the door.
'You're the kid with the encyclopedia,' he says. 'We'd like to borrow it.' You ask who 'we' is. He smiles. 'The people trying to keep the lights on.'

science.claim: You can download all of English Wikipedia, with pictures, to a phone: about 100 GB.
science.working: Kiwix publishes the full English Wikipedia with images ('maxi') as a single ZIM file of roughly 100-110 GB, readable offline on phones and computers; English Wikipedia has nearly 7 million articles.
